new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level (Mixe branch) generalization: primary stress sits on the final syllable of the last root of the word; prefixes and suffixes are not stressed. The author's data explicitly include Mazatlán ('Coatlán, Guichicovi y Mazatlán (mixe bajo)'), but the sentence is not stated for Mazatlán in particular and its immediate scope ('en todos estos casos') is the compound/serial verb examples in (15). Sibling Lowland Mixe descriptions on file give compatible root-final rules: Isthmus Mixe (Mogoñé Viejo) final-syllable stress with a list of unstressed ë-suffixes (Dieterman & McCarty 2018: 141-142); Coatlán Mixe final syllable if C-final or long-V-final, else penult, with three stress-carrying suffixes (Hoogshagen 1984: 5).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the captured snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: None captured for the Mixe branch statement; the Isthmus Mixe dictionary (different language) lists never-stressed suffixes with simple ë, and Coatlán Mixe has stress-carrying suffixes -yi, -i, -o'k.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (polymorphemic verb forms); snippet gives no citation-form or phrase-level qualification.
new_statements.identity_note: Target is Mazatlán Mixe [maza1292 / mzl] (San Juan Mazatlán, 'Tutla Mixe'), a Lowland Mixe language distinct from Isthmus/Guichicovi Mixe [mir, isth1238] and Coatlán Mixe [mco, coat1238]. The earlier scan's source (Dieterman 2008) describes Isthmus Mixe of Mogoñé Viejo/San Juan Guichicovi, not Mazatlán. The quoted Romero Méndez 2018 statement is a Mixe-branch generalization whose data pool includes Mazatlán but is not a Mazatlán-specific description. Glottolog's single mzl reference (Bickford 1984) appears from snippets to be a pan-Mixe historical-vowel paper with no visible Mazatlán data.

sources.citation: Dieterman, Julia & James Michael McCarty Jr. (comps.). 2018. Breve diccionario del mixe del Istmo, Mogoñé Viejo, Oaxaca. (VDI Mariano Silva y Aceves 52.) México: ILV. §A.12 El acento, pp. 141-142.
sources.note: DIFFERENT LANGUAGE (Isthmus/Guichicovi Mixe mir = isth1238), same Lowland branch: 'En la variante de Mogoñé Viejo, las palabras que tienen más de una sílaba... llevan un acento prosódico en la última sílaba. Como el acento prosódico es predecible, no es necesario escribir el acento ortográfico.... Al parecer, en las otras lenguas mixes de la región baja, tampoco se escribe el acento ortográfico.' plus a short list of never-stressed suffixes with simple ë (-ë, -ëch, -ëk, -ëts, -ëm, -ën, -ëp).

sources.citation: Romero-Méndez, Rodrigo. 2008. A Reference Grammar of Ayutla Mixe. PhD diss., SUNY Buffalo.
sources.note: Mazatlán appears only in the classification list 'Lowland Mixe (Camotlán, Coatlán, Mazatlán, and Guichicovi Mixe)'; its stress section (§3.7) is Ayutla-specific.

sources.citation: Hoogshagen, Searle. 1984. Coatlán Mixe. In Supplement to the Handbook of Middle American Indians 2: Linguistics, 3-19. Austin: UT Press.
sources.note: DIFFERENT LANGUAGE (Coatlán Mixe mco = coat1238): final syllable of an uninflected word ending in C or long V, else penult; stem-final in inflected words unless a stress-carrying suffix (-yi, -i, -o'k) is present (§1.3, p. 5). Not about Mazatlán.

sources.citation: Romero Méndez, Rodrigo. 2015. Multidialectal orthography and the writing of vowels in Mixe. ICLDC 4 slides, 8 pp. University of Hawaii ScholarSpace.
sources.note: No placement rule; only a 'Non stressed vowels' vowel chart (Ayutla vs Coatlán). Lowland data are Guichicovi/Coatlán; Mazatlán not mentioned.

sources.citation: Bickford, J. Albert. 1985. Fortis/lenis consonants in Guichicovi Mixe: a preliminary acoustic study. Work Papers SIL-UND 29: 195-207.
sources.note: Silent on stress placement. Mentions Mazatlán only as a dialect where the author has 'heard what appears to be the same [fortis/lenis] contrast... the third main Eastern dialect of Mixe' (p. 196) and as needing study (p. 206).
